text:
support-agent: Escalation from acme-platform — customer sees intermittent 502/504s from hosted API during key rotations. Started ~08:22 UTC, ~10% of requests failing for a few mins. Trace ids: trace=4b9f..., trace=7c1a...
support-agent: Customer says failures correlate with automated key rotation window and retry loops from their side. They sent curl repro.
acme-platform: Repro steps: curl -v https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <rotating-token>" -H "X-Request-ID: acme-1234" --data '{"prompt":"hi"}' --max-time 10
acme-platform: When we hit during rotation we get: HTTP/2 504, then some 502s. We see Envoy upstream reset in our sidecar logs.
ivan.sre: Thanks — looking at edge metrics now. Noted short spike at 08:21:40 UTC in upstream_5xx_rate and h2_stream_reset_count. Can you paste the customer trace ids?
support-agent: pasted above — 4b9f... and 7c1a... also customer attached envoy access logs snippet: 
```
[2026-01-12T08:21:41.123Z] "POST /v1/generate" 502 0 0 17 0 "-" "python-requests/2.28" x-forwarded-for: 10.12.5.4 - upstream_service: inference-hostpool-2
[2026-01-12T08:21:42.789Z] "POST /v1/generate" 504 0 0 23 0 "-" "curl/7.85" x-forwarded-for: 10.12.5.4 - upstream_service: inference-hostpool-2
```
ivan.sre: Envoy logs show upstream connection failure + h2 RST_STREAM. Possible upstream instance cycling while key refresh hits auth tier.
sarah.runtime: On our side, auth-service reported a short surge of 503s to token-verify endpoint at 08:21:40 due to a concurrent KMS rotation job. Some token validations timed out ~300-500ms and caused backpressure on the auth connection pool. We also saw increased 429->retry behavior from clients.
kevin.prod: Customer-facing churn during rotation is bad. Is this because we don't drain auth caches while rotating keys? Any mitigation we can do short-term?
emily.cs: Acme is threatening to pause traffic if we can't guarantee rotation-safe flows. Need ETA and mitigations.
sarah.runtime: Short-term: add a soft-stall/queue at auth-proxy so we return 503 with Retry-After instead of dropping connections to upstream inference. Longer-term: make token verifier accept previous key for X minutes (grace window) and increase auth pool size during rotation.
ivan.sre: Immediate mitigation we can try: 1) bump auth-proxy connect timeout from 250ms->750ms for the next rotation window, 2) temporarily mark a small subset of edge nodes to prefer cached-verified tokens. I'll coordinate with deploy-bot.
deploy-bot: Scheduled runtime change: auth-proxy timeout bump -> rollout in 2m; target: prod-edge pool subset. CI checks passed.
acme-platform: We'll hold off scaling down our client retries for now but can add exponential backoff. Can you provide exact repro window so we correlate logs?
support-agent: Window was 08:21:35 - 08:23:10 UTC. Please check trace=4b9f... and trace=7c1a... in the logging ingestion.
ivan.sre: Confirmed traces show 502 at proxy->inference with upstream reset (reason: connection failure). Auth-service 503s spike aligns to 08:21:40. Deployed timeout bump — monitoring.
sarah.runtime: Also surfaced a small bug: during rotation our auth-cache eviction runs synchronously which briefly blocks verifier threads. Patch ready: change eviction to async and add config toggle. Can push as hotfix if needed.
kevin.prod: Push hotfix to canary ASAP after timeout bump stabilizes. Notify acme and set rotation window to low-traffic time.
emily.cs: I'll update acme and propose scheduled rotation at 02:00 UTC and share mitigations.
support-agent: For postmortem: collect auth-proxy traces, KMS rotation job logs, envoy upstream reset traces, and client retry patterns. Assign to eng-runtime + eng-sre.
ivan.sre: I'll own the incident ticket. Tagging #eng-runtime for hotfix.
sarah.runtime: Thanks — prepping PR for async eviction and grace-key acceptance. Will link PR.
acme-platform: Thanks all. Appreciate the quick response. We'll retest once you confirm the fix. :thumbsup:
